name: Deployment, Images & Operations
purpose: Ship and run the platform: the pinned CPU/GPU/edge/demo image definitions, hardened Compose recipes, the systemd unit, production deployment documentation and the disposable-container smoke tests that gate an image before it is called deployable.

public_interfaces.name: CPU runtime image (sentinelzone-ai:standalone)
public_interfaces.contract: Serves the app on :8000 with no camera configured; credentials, keys and weights are not baked in.

public_interfaces.name: Hardened Compose recipe
public_interfaces.contract: Read-only root filesystem, dropped capabilities, no-new-privileges, named data volume and pinned environment contract.

public_interfaces.name: SSH-tunnel Compose overlay
public_interfaces.contract: Adds the camera tunnel path for RTSP smoke tests without exposing the tunnel beyond loopback.

public_interfaces.name: systemd edge unit
public_interfaces.contract: Runs the container on an edge host with restart-on-failure and explicit environment file.

public_interfaces.name: single-instance identity (compose project/container/volume names)
public_interfaces.contract: Pins project name 'sentinelzone', container name 'sentinelzone' and volume 'sentinelzone-state' so a second stack from another checkout fails loudly instead of running a duplicate that fights for host port 8000.

public_interfaces.name: duplicate-instance audit (read-only)
public_interfaces.contract: Lists every container from the SentinelZone images with its supervisor, restart policy and published ports; exits 1 when two containers do the same job or contest one host port, and prints remediation without ever mutating anything.

public_interfaces.name: single-instance fix (dry run by default)
public_interfaces.contract: Plans the removal of every duplicate container, clears its restart policy before removal (docker update --restart=no then docker rm -f), never touches the container named with --keep, optionally tears down a duplicate Compose stack, re-audits afterwards, and executes nothing without --apply.

runtime_dependencies: requirements-runtime.lock (pinned by the shared platform scope)
acceptance_criteria: docker build -f Dockerfile succeeds and the image answers /health.
The Compose recipe starts with a read-only root and a writable data volume.
The three smoke scripts each bootstrap and tear down their own disposable resources.
No image bakes in camera credentials, SSH keys or private setup data.
Exactly one container from this image is supervised on a host: a second compose project or docker run cannot silently coexist (pinned names).
scripts/docker_instance_audit.py reports OK on a healthy host, names the supervisor of every container, and never mutates anything.
scripts/docker_single_instance_fix.py is a dry run by default, clears restart policies before removal, leaves the --keep container untouched, and verifies the result by re-auditing.
risks: Image builds need network access for the pinned wheels; the sandbox used for the decomposition could not build or run them.
Four Dockerfiles plus four Compose files drift easily; the smoke scripts are the only automated coupling between them.
requirements-runtime.txt/.lock stay in the shared platform scope, so a dependency bump is a cross-project change.

Observed on a site host: two containers from the same image, both with restart policies and both publishing 8000, alternate ownership of the port and look like a flapping deployment. The pinned names stop the repository from recreating that; a duplicate started by hand, cron or another unit must still be found and removed (deploy/SINGLE_INSTANCE.md).
Pinning container_name disables `docker compose up --scale`, deliberately: a second worker would open a duplicate camera connection.
